before.title: The passive Lorentz boost with parameter beta
before.statement: Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame of the model (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), and let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be its coordinates, so that a vector is written x = x^0 e_0 + x^1 e_1 + x^2 e_2 + x^3 e_3 and the spatial part is the coordinate column x_vec = (x^1,x^2,x^3) of R^3 with its standard Euclidean structure (def-euclidean-inner-product). For beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1, where |beta| is the Euclidean norm, set gamma(beta) := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2) > 1 (def-rational-power, lem-rational-power-laws). The passive Lorentz boost with parameter beta is the linear map B(beta): V -> V defined by its action on coordinates: for beta not equal to 0, x'^0 = gamma (x^0 - beta . x),  x' = x + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . x) beta - gamma beta x^0, and for beta = 0, B(0) := identity, where x' denotes the coordinates of B(beta) applied to the vector with coordinates x, and beta . x is the Euclidean scalar product. Equivalently, in the ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) the matrix of B(beta) is B^0_0 = gamma, B^0_i = B^i_0 = -gamma beta_i for i = 1,2,3, and B^i_j = delta^i_j + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) beta_i beta_j for i,j = 1,2,3 (with the last expression replaced by delta^i_j for beta = 0; its beta -> 0 limit is (1/2) beta_i beta_j). In the 1+1 case beta = beta e_1 this reads x'^0 = gamma(x^0 - beta x^1), x'^1 = gamma(x^1 - beta x^0). The vector beta is called the boost parameter; it is dimensionless and mathematically independent of any unit convention.
before.strategy: A definition item, well-defined because the displayed formulas assign to every coordinate pair (x^0,x_vec) a pair (x'^0,x'_vec), and by thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis (applied through def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map) there is a unique linear map with that matrix, namely x |-> E o M o E^{-1}. The beta = 0 case is declared separately because the matrix expression ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) is undefined there; the definition must not silently divide by zero, and the extension is not asserted to be continuous (that is a separate computation). This item asserts no Lorentz property: that B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map and that B(-beta) is its inverse is the content of lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, and the composition law is the content of lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition; the physical reading of c beta as a relative velocity is stated only on the physics items of this page, not here.

after.title: The passive Lorentz boost with parameter beta
after.statement: Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame of the model (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), and let x = (x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3) be its coordinates, so that a vector is written x = x^0 e_0 + x^1 e_1 + x^2 e_2 + x^3 e_3 and the spatial part is the coordinate column x_vec = (x^1,x^2,x^3) of R^3 with its standard Euclidean structure (def-euclidean-inner-product). For beta in R^3 with |beta| < 1, where |beta| is the Euclidean norm, set gamma(beta) := (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2) >= 1, with equality exactly for beta=0 and strict inequality for beta!=0 (def-rational-power, lem-rational-power-laws). The passive Lorentz boost with parameter beta is the linear map B(beta): V -> V defined by its action on coordinates: for beta not equal to 0, x'^0 = gamma (x^0 - beta . x),  x' = x + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2)(beta . x) beta - gamma beta x^0, and for beta = 0, B(0) := identity, where x' denotes the coordinates of B(beta) applied to the vector with coordinates x, and beta . x is the Euclidean scalar product. Equivalently, in the ordered basis (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) the matrix of B(beta) is B^0_0 = gamma, B^0_i = B^i_0 = -gamma beta_i for i = 1,2,3, and B^i_j = delta^i_j + ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) beta_i beta_j for i,j = 1,2,3 (with the last expression replaced by delta^i_j for beta = 0; the coefficient (gamma−1)/|beta|^2 tends to 1/2 as beta tends to0 through nonzero vectors, so the correction is (1/2) beta_i beta_j+o(|beta|^2) and the full spatial block tends to delta^i_j). In the 1+1 case beta = beta e_1 this reads x'^0 = gamma(x^0 - beta x^1), x'^1 = gamma(x^1 - beta x^0). The vector beta is called the boost parameter; it is dimensionless and mathematically independent of any unit convention.
after.strategy: A definition item, well-defined because the displayed formulas assign to every coordinate pair (x^0,x_vec) a pair (x'^0,x'_vec), and by thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis (applied through def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map) there is a unique linear map with that matrix, namely x |-> E o M o E^{-1}. The beta = 0 case is declared separately because the matrix expression ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) is undefined there; the definition must not silently divide by zero, and the stated limit follows from the explicit rationalization below. This item asserts no Lorentz property: that B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map and that B(-beta) is its inverse is the content of lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, and the composition law is the content of lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition; the physical reading of c beta as a relative velocity is stated only on the physics items of this page, not here. For the gamma boundary, gamma is positive and gamma^2=1/(1−|beta|^2)>=1, with equality exactly when |beta|=0, so gamma>=1 with precisely the asserted equality case. For beta!=0 the identity gamma^2−1=|beta|^2 gamma^2 yields (gamma−1)/|beta|^2=gamma^2/(gamma+1). Continuity of the positive power in [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] makes gamma tend to1 as beta tends to0, hence that coefficient tends to1/2. Multiplication by beta_i beta_j proves the leading correction and full spatial-block limit: |beta_i beta_j|<=|beta|^2, so [gamma^2/(gamma+1)−1/2]beta_i beta_j=o(|beta|^2). Thus B(beta) tends to the separately declared identity without a hidden division by zero. No physical velocity interpretation is added. Real and rational powers are identified by [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]]. The Euclidean norm convention gives $|\beta_i|^2\le\sum_k\beta_k^2=|\beta|^2$, hence $|\beta_i|\le|\beta|$ and $|\beta_i\beta_j|\le|\beta|^2$. In the norm meaning of $\beta\to0$, $|\beta|\to0$. For $|\beta|^2\le3/4$ one has $1\le\gamma\le2$, so $|\gamma\beta_i|\le2|\beta|\to0$; also $\gamma-1=|\beta|^2\gamma^2/(\gamma+1)\to0$. Together with the already proved spatial-block limit these are every matrix entry of $B(\beta)\to I$.
